FINIS, Inc. is an American manufacturer of swim training and pool equipment,
founded in 1993 in Northern California by John Mix and Pablo Morales, the 1992
Olympic champion in the 100 metre butterfly, and now based in Livermore,
California.[^story][^jobspec] The company says the name is the Latin word for
"the end" or "grand finale", chosen because it contains the word "fin", its
first product, and evokes the finish of a race.[^owp] Unlike the timing-system
vendors covered elsewhere in this wiki, FINIS makes training tools and
unpowered pool equipment rather than electronics for officiating; its product
documented in the [equipment reference](../equipment/index.md) is the
[Backstroke Start Wedge](../equipment/swimming/backstroke-start/finis.md).

## History

John Mix first encountered a monofin during a semester abroad in Austria in 1988
and returned to the United States convinced of its value as a training tool for
competitive swimmers.[^story][^owp] After Morales, a high-school friend and
teammate, won gold in the 100 metre butterfly at the 1992 Barcelona Games, the
two founded FINIS Incorporated in 1993 under the direction of John's oldest
brother, Jerry Mix Jr., and built the first FINIS monofin, a rubber foot pocket
mounted on a single fiberglass blade, in a garage.[^story][^captyn]

The Swimmer's Snorkel followed in 1995, a center-mount snorkel designed for the
competitive swim market; FINIS credits early validation of the design to
University of California-Berkeley coach Nort Thornton.[^story] The company
states that its product philosophy has stayed technique-first: co-founder John
Mix has said the company is "only going to build a product if it's going to
have a specific purpose of improving technique".[^sw30] FINIS opened its first
international office in 2010 to serve Europe, the Middle East, and North
Africa.[^story]

## Products

FINIS designs training equipment for competitive and fitness swimming. Dated
milestones from the company's own history include the monofin (1993), the
Swimmer's Snorkel (1995), the Tech Toc and Hydro Hip rotation trainers (1996),
the Tempo Trainer pacing device (2001), the Agility paddle (2012, which FINIS
describes as the first strapless paddle on the market), the Axis buoy and Duo
underwater audio player (2015), the Smart Goggle (2021), and the Manta paddle
(2022).[^story] Its underwater audio products, including the earlier SwiMP3 and
Neptune, transmit sound through bone conduction.[^owp]

On the pool-equipment side, FINIS sells the
[Backstroke Start Wedge](../equipment/swimming/backstroke-start/finis.md), a
manual backstroke start device developed in collaboration with Vince Harris of
WEDG Swim Start Systems of County Cork, Ireland.[^wedge] That article covers the
device in full; the
[backstroke start devices overview](../equipment/swimming/backstroke-start/index.md)
covers the equipment class and its rules.

## In competition

FINIS describes the Backstroke Start Wedge as compliant with the World Aquatics
(FINA) facilities rules and usable in both training and competition.[^wedge]
More broadly, the company's training products are marketed for practice rather
than officiating; Openwaterpedia states that FINIS products are used by US and
international Olympic teams, triathletes, and fitness swimmers.[^owp]
